messages:
katy: uploaded perfetto trace for the 11:02 P99 spike: https://perfetto.local/trace/1919991234
katy: quick summary: client->gateway spans look usual, gateway queue wait jumps ~80ms, but runtime timeline shows a kernel-select flip for the same requests — large-batch matmul chosen then swapped to small-batch, adding ~60ms tail per token
mike: can you paste kernel names / nvtx markers you saw in the runtime trace?
katy: from the runtime NVTX timeline (copied from trace):
```
nvtx: kernel_select:start
nvtx: kernel=matmul_large_batch
nvtx: kernel_swap:decision -> matmul_small_batch
nvtx: kvcache:miss
nvtx: run_kernel:matmul_small_batch
nvtx: kernel_select:end
```
katy: note ordering: the swap happens immediately after a burst of KV cache misses (new prefixes). That aligns with the client burst of short initial tokens which skewed the selection heuristic
anita: how many concurrent inflight requests and observed batch sizes during the window?
katy: concurrency ~18. Batch size distribution sampled on the worker during spike: 1-3 tokens/request = 60%, 4-7 = 30%, 8+ = 10%. The affected flows were mostly 1-2 token inits interleaved with longer sessions — short seq burst biased the moving window
mike: our selection policy looks at a short moving window of seq_len distribution per worker, right? If that window fills with short sequences it will prefer the small-batch kernel even though aggregated batches could be large
katy: exactly. Current window length = 50 requests. The KV miss burst (many cold prefixes) produced many short inits within that window and triggered the flip
dave: can we reproduce locally with nsys + controlled prefills? If KV miss + short-seq burst reliably causes swap we can iterate on mitigations
anita: suggested repro command (keeps interleaving deterministic with --seed):
```
# repro script (approx)
./bench_client --concurrency 18 --prefill 70 --short-bursts 8 --kv-miss-rate 0.45 --seed 42
# profile runtime with NVTX capture
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_kernelselect --trace=nvtx --sample=none ./runtime_server --config test_kernelselect.yaml
```
mike: if we can repro, we should add a metric that emits kernel selection churn/sec and emit NVTX event when hysteresis blocks a flip
katy: logged TODO in tracker: expose `kernel_select_churn` gauge, add `kernel_select_reason` NVTX tag (e.g., "kvcache_miss" vs "latency_slo"), and emit an enum when fallback chosen
perf-bot: Regression alert: P99 token latency +4.2% in 11:01:50-11:03:10. Correlated with kernel_selection swap events at 11:01:56. Linked perfetto: https://perfetto.local/trace/1919991234
dave: quick mitigation idea: add hysteresis to selection so we require N consecutive small-window signals before switching, or prefer current kernel for X ms unless miss ratio > Y
anita: hysteresis is low-risk. propose initial params: N=3 consecutive signals and sticky_duration=200ms. We can A/B via runtime flag first
mike: also update batching heuristic: if current accumulated batch_size >= 4 prefer large-batch kernel regardless of window signal. That's conservative and aligns with throughput vs latency tradeoff
katy: opened PR draft with hysteresis + new metric + NVTX marker: https://git.internal/r/3204 (WIP). Test plan in PR: repro, nsys capture, perfetto diff vs golden, land behind flag, canary for 24h
mike: will add a small CI perf job to run matmul_small/large microbench comparisons to ensure we don't regress tail on cold paths
katy: I ran a quick local nsys run using the repro above. Short summary from CUDA timeline: small_batch kernel has ~1.8ms extra launch overhead per invocation, large_batch kernel amortizes launch cost but has ~10-12ms compute depending on batch dims. When swapped mid-flow we see a gap: worker drains queued large-batch work, then small kernel launches cause serialized work leading to token tail
anita: send the nsys report gist and I can parse kernel durations + SM utilization; need to confirm if workspace allocation / cudnn heuristics differ between kernels
katy: gist: https://gist.internal/katy/nsys-kernelselect-191999 (contains nvprof-like breakdown + nvtx markers)
dave: testing mitigation locally: I patched selection to require 2 consecutive small signals before swap and added sticky_duration=150ms. On the repro load P99 dropped ~2.6% and kernel_select swap rate dropped 54%
mike: good signal. Next: land behind flag, run CI perf tests, then canary. Also add a Prometheus rule to alert if `kernel_select_churn > 5/s` for 1m
katy: adding perfetto query snippet to rapidly filter relevant ranges:
```
-- perfetto filter snippet
event.name CONTAINS 'kernel_select' OR event.name CONTAINS 'kvcache'
track.name CONTAINS 'gateway' OR track.name CONTAINS 'runtime_worker'
```
mike: small ops: 1) add NVTX tags for reason (kvcache_miss vs latency_slo) 2) expose churn gauge 3) land hysteresis flag 4) CI microbench 5) canary + 24h watch
anita: once you have nsys output, I can help map kernel SM occupancy and PMA stalls. small/large kernel differences may be due to workspace allocation or cublas algorithm pick
katy: thanks — I'll post nsys tarball + perfetto links here when done. If the canary looks good we'll promote to stable and then consider raising the default window size from 50->75 as longer window reduces sensitivity to short bursts
dave: agree. If hysteresis <-> batching-favor approach reduces P99 we can avoid widening window which might delay legitimate switches
katy: thanks all — will update this thread with artifacts and the PR link. Leaving action items pinned in tracker. :thumbsup:
